Create CTL2 for a Reformat/Map component. It has one input port (0) and one output port (0); use the Reformat entry point.

Input metadata, port 0:
<Metadata id="SubscriptionUsageIn">
  <Record name="SubscriptionUsageIn_Record" type="delimited">
    <Field name="account_id" type="string" nullable="false"/>
    <Field name="billing_period_start" type="date" format="yyyy-MM-dd" nullable="false"/>
    <Field name="plan_code" type="string" nullable="false"/>
    <Field name="active_seats" type="integer" nullable="false"/>
    <Field name="included_api_calls" type="long" nullable="false"/>
    <Field name="actual_api_calls" type="long" nullable="false"/>
    <Field name="storage_gb" type="decimal" nullable="false"/>
    <Field name="is_nonprofit" type="boolean" nullable="false"/>
    <Field name="payment_status" type="string" nullable="false"/>
    <Field name="contract_discount_pct" type="decimal"/>
  </Record>
</Metadata>

Output metadata, port 0:
<Metadata id="SubscriptionInvoiceOut">
  <Record name="SubscriptionInvoiceOut_Record" type="delimited">
    <Field name="account_id" type="string" nullable="false"/>
    <Field name="invoice_period" type="string" nullable="false"/>
    <Field name="due_date" type="date" format="yyyy-MM-dd" nullable="false"/>
    <Field name="seat_charge" type="decimal" nullable="false"/>
    <Field name="usage_charge" type="decimal" nullable="false"/>
    <Field name="storage_charge" type="decimal" nullable="false"/>
    <Field name="discount_amount" type="decimal" nullable="false"/>
    <Field name="tax_amount" type="decimal" nullable="false"/>
    <Field name="amount_due" type="decimal" nullable="false"/>
    <Field name="collection_action" type="string" nullable="false"/>
  </Record>
</Metadata>

Business logic:
- The invoice period is the calendar month of billing_period_start formatted as yyyy-MM. Due date is 15 days after billing_period_start.
- Monthly seat price is 49.00 for STARTER, 89.00 for GROWTH, and 149.00 for ENTERPRISE. Any other plan is charged at the STARTER rate.
- Charge 0.0025 per API call above included_api_calls. Negative overage must be treated as zero.
- Storage is free through 50 GB; each GB above 50 costs 0.18.
- The contract discount is contract_discount_pct of the subtotal (seats + usage + storage). A null discount means zero. Nonprofits receive an additional 10% discount of the subtotal, but total discount may not exceed 35% of subtotal.
- Tax is 0 for nonprofits. For all others, tax is 20% of subtotal less discount. Round every monetary output to two decimals, and calculate amount_due from the rounded charge, discount, and tax values.
- collection_action is HOLD when payment_status is SUSPENDED, REVIEW when amount_due is greater than 5000, and COLLECT otherwise. Return the record on the sole output port.

Implementation clarifications:
- All named values are fields in the input record: plan_code selects the seat rate; active_seats is multiplied by that rate; actual_api_calls and included_api_calls determine overage; storage_gb determines storage charges; is_nonprofit controls the nonprofit discount and tax; payment_status controls HOLD.
- subtotal means the unrounded sum of seat_charge, usage_charge, and storage_charge. contract_discount_pct is a percentage value such as 12.5 for 12.5%, not a fraction. Apply the 35% cap to the combined contract and nonprofit discounts.
- For non-nonprofits, tax is 20% of (subtotal - discount_amount). The output monetary fields are rounded individually to two decimal places before amount_due is calculated as rounded seat_charge + rounded usage_charge + rounded storage_charge - rounded discount_amount + rounded tax_amount.
- collection_action precedence is payment_status is SUSPENDED first, then amount_due > 5000, then COLLECT.

Write the CTL2 transformation for a Reformat/Map component with input port 0 and output port 0.

Input metadata, port 0:
<Metadata id="MarketplaceOrderIn">
  <Record name="MarketplaceOrderIn_Record" type="delimited">
    <Field name="order_id" type="string" nullable="false"/>
    <Field name="order_timestamp" type="date" format="yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss" nullable="false"/>
    <Field name="country_code" type="string" nullable="false"/>
    <Field name="shipping_service" type="string" nullable="false"/>
    <Field name="item_count" type="integer" nullable="false"/>
    <Field name="total_weight_kg" type="decimal" nullable="false"/>
    <Field name="order_total" type="decimal" nullable="false"/>
    <Field name="address_line1" type="string"/>
    <Field name="address_line2" type="string"/>
    <Field name="postal_code" type="string"/>
    <Field name="is_hazmat" type="boolean" nullable="false"/>
  </Record>
</Metadata>

Lookup metadata: `CountryFulfillmentLookup` is keyed by country_code and returns country_code (string), warehouse_code (string), standard_transit_days (integer), express_transit_days (integer), and remote_area_postal_prefixes (string list). The lookup has at most one row per key.

Output metadata, port 0:
<Metadata id="FulfillmentInstructionOut">
  <Record name="FulfillmentInstructionOut_Record" type="delimited">
    <Field name="order_id" type="string" nullable="false"/>
    <Field name="warehouse_code" type="string" nullable="false"/>
    <Field name="service_level" type="string" nullable="false"/>
    <Field name="ship_by" type="date" format="yyyy-MM-dd" nullable="false"/>
    <Field name="promised_delivery" type="date" format="yyyy-MM-dd" nullable="false"/>
    <Field name="package_class" type="string" nullable="false"/>
    <Field name="address_status" type="string" nullable="false"/>
    <Field name="manual_review_reason" type="string"/>
  </Record>
</Metadata>

Business logic:
- Retrieve the country lookup record using country_code. If it is missing, set warehouse_code to UNKNOWN, service_level to MANUAL, ship_by and promised_delivery to the order date, package_class to UNKNOWN, address_status to COUNTRY_NOT_CONFIGURED, and manual_review_reason to COUNTRY_NOT_CONFIGURED.
- Otherwise use the lookup warehouse. EXPRESS stays EXPRESS only when item_count is at most 20 and total_weight_kg is at most 25; otherwise downgrade it to STANDARD. HAZMAT orders must use GROUND, regardless of the requested service.
- ship_by is the order date plus 0 days for EXPRESS, 1 day for STANDARD, and 2 days for GROUND. promised_delivery is ship_by plus the corresponding lookup transit days; GROUND uses standard transit days plus 2.
- package_class is ENVELOPE for exactly one item at or below 0.5 kg, PARCEL for weight up to 20 kg, FREIGHT for heavier orders, and HAZMAT_FREIGHT for any hazmat order heavier than 20 kg.
- An address is INCOMPLETE if address_line1 or postal_code is null or empty. Otherwise it is REMOTE when postal_code begins with any configured remote-area prefix, and VALID in all other cases. A remote address adds 2 days to promised_delivery.
- manual_review_reason is HAZMAT_REMOTE when both conditions apply, ADDRESS_INCOMPLETE for an incomplete address, WEIGHT_LIMIT when total_weight_kg exceeds 70, and null when none apply. When several conditions apply, use the first reason in the order just listed. Emit one record.

Implementation clarifications:
- Use country_code as the key to CountryFulfillmentLookup. The order date means the calendar-date portion of order_timestamp. The requested service is shipping_service and the hazmat flag is is_hazmat.
- Use express_transit_days only for effective service EXPRESS. Use standard_transit_days for effective service STANDARD, and standard_transit_days + 2 for effective service GROUND. Apply the remote-address two-day addition after this transit calculation.
- For the REMOTE test, compare postal_code against each string in the lookup field remote_area_postal_prefixes; an absent or empty prefix list has no match. Address status precedence is INCOMPLETE before REMOTE before VALID.
- manual_review_reason conditions use is_hazmat with address_status REMOTE, address_status INCOMPLETE, and total_weight_kg > 70, in the stated precedence order.

Lookup table definition:
- Lookup table ID: CountryFulfillmentLookup.
- Lookup record metadata ID: CountryFulfillmentLookupMeta.
- Lookup record name: CountryFulfillmentLookup_Record.
- Key field(s): country_code.
- Fields: country_code:string; warehouse_code:string; standard_transit_days:integer; express_transit_days:integer; remote_area_postal_prefixes:string[].

Produce CTL2 for a Reformat/Map component that reads port 0 and writes port 0.

Input metadata, port 0:
<Metadata id="LeaveRequestIn">
  <Record name="LeaveRequestIn_Record" type="delimited">
    <Field name="employee_id" type="string" nullable="false"/>
    <Field name="employment_type" type="string" nullable="false"/>
    <Field name="hire_date" type="date" format="yyyy-MM-dd" nullable="false"/>
    <Field name="request_date" type="date" format="yyyy-MM-dd" nullable="false"/>
    <Field name="leave_start" type="date" format="yyyy-MM-dd" nullable="false"/>
    <Field name="leave_end" type="date" format="yyyy-MM-dd" nullable="false"/>
    <Field name="leave_type" type="string" nullable="false"/>
    <Field name="requested_hours" type="decimal" nullable="false"/>
    <Field name="available_pto_hours" type="decimal" nullable="false"/>
    <Field name="manager_approved" type="boolean" nullable="false"/>
    <Field name="medical_certificate_received" type="boolean" nullable="false"/>
  </Record>
</Metadata>

Output metadata, port 0:
<Metadata id="LeaveDecisionOut">
  <Record name="LeaveDecisionOut_Record" type="delimited">
    <Field name="employee_id" type="string" nullable="false"/>
    <Field name="leave_type" type="string" nullable="false"/>
    <Field name="service_years" type="integer" nullable="false"/>
    <Field name="calendar_days_requested" type="integer" nullable="false"/>
    <Field name="approved_hours" type="decimal" nullable="false"/>
    <Field name="remaining_pto_hours" type="decimal" nullable="false"/>
    <Field name="decision" type="string" nullable="false"/>
    <Field name="decision_reason" type="string" nullable="false"/>
    <Field name="requires_hr_review" type="boolean" nullable="false"/>
  </Record>
</Metadata>

Business logic:
- service_years is the whole-year difference between request_date and hire_date; do not allow a negative result. calendar_days_requested is the inclusive date span from leave_start through leave_end; use zero when leave_end precedes leave_start.
- For CONTRACTOR employees, approve zero hours and set decision to REJECTED with reason CONTRACTOR_NOT_ELIGIBLE.
- For PTO, reject with INVALID_DATE_RANGE when the span is zero; reject with MANAGER_APPROVAL_REQUIRED when manager_approved is false; otherwise approve the lower of requested_hours and available_pto_hours. If only part can be approved, decision is PARTIALLY_APPROVED with reason INSUFFICIENT_PTO; if all requested hours can be approved, decision is APPROVED with reason PTO_AVAILABLE.
- For SICK leave, approve all requested hours when the date range is valid. A medical certificate is required only for spans longer than 3 calendar days: without it, decision is PENDING and approved_hours is zero with reason MEDICAL_CERTIFICATE_REQUIRED.
- For BEREAVEMENT leave, approve up to 24 hours regardless of PTO balance when manager-approved; otherwise it is PENDING with reason MANAGER_APPROVAL_REQUIRED.
- Any unrecognized leave_type is REJECTED with reason UNSUPPORTED_LEAVE_TYPE. remaining_pto_hours is available_pto_hours minus approved_hours only for PTO; it is unchanged for every other leave type. Round the two hour values to two decimals. requires_hr_review is true for any request exceeding 80 hours, a PTO request with more than 40 unapproved hours, or a sick-leave request pending a certificate. Emit one record.

Implementation clarifications:
- Employment eligibility is determined only by employment_type: CONTRACTOR is ineligible; every other value follows the leave-type rules. Leave category is determined only by leave_type (PTO, SICK, or BEREAVEMENT).
- Evaluate the CONTRACTOR rule before every leave-type rule. For non-contractors, a zero calendar_days_requested is an invalid range for every supported leave_type and produces REJECTED / INVALID_DATE_RANGE with approved_hours 0.
- The manager approval condition uses manager_approved; the certificate condition uses medical_certificate_received. PTO balance and the more-than-40-unapproved-hours HR rule use available_pto_hours and requested_hours.
- For all rejected or pending outcomes, remaining_pto_hours follows the existing rule: only a PTO outcome subtracts approved_hours; non-PTO leaves retain available_pto_hours.

Create a CTL2 Reformat/Map transformation with one input port and two output ports. Return the correct output port for each record.

Input metadata, port 0:
<Metadata id="CustomerActivityIn">
  <Record name="CustomerActivityIn_Record" type="delimited">
    <Field name="customer_id" type="string" nullable="false"/>
    <Field name="event_time" type="date" format="yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss" nullable="false"/>
    <Field name="country_code" type="string" nullable="false"/>
    <Field name="device_id" type="string"/>
    <Field name="failed_login_count_24h" type="integer" nullable="false"/>
    <Field name="chargeback_count_180d" type="integer" nullable="false"/>
    <Field name="transaction_amount" type="decimal" nullable="false"/>
    <Field name="account_age_days" type="integer" nullable="false"/>
    <Field name="is_vpn_detected" type="boolean" nullable="false"/>
  </Record>
</Metadata>

Lookup metadata: `CountryRiskLookup`, keyed by country_code, returns country_code (string), base_risk_points (integer), high_risk_amount_threshold (decimal), and embargoed (boolean). It has at most one matching record.

Output metadata, port 0 (manual-review queue):
<Metadata id="ManualReviewOut">
  <Record name="ManualReviewOut_Record" type="delimited">
    <Field name="customer_id" type="string" nullable="false"/>
    <Field name="risk_score" type="integer" nullable="false"/>
    <Field name="risk_band" type="string" nullable="false"/>
    <Field name="primary_reason" type="string" nullable="false"/>
    <Field name="event_date" type="date" format="yyyy-MM-dd" nullable="false"/>
    <Field name="masked_device_id" type="string" nullable="false"/>
  </Record>
</Metadata>

Output metadata, port 1 (auto-clear audit):
<Metadata id="AutoClearOut">
  <Record name="AutoClearOut_Record" type="delimited">
    <Field name="customer_id" type="string" nullable="false"/>
    <Field name="risk_score" type="integer" nullable="false"/>
    <Field name="risk_band" type="string" nullable="false"/>
    <Field name="clearance_code" type="string" nullable="false"/>
    <Field name="event_date" type="date" format="yyyy-MM-dd" nullable="false"/>
  </Record>
</Metadata>

Business logic:
- A missing country lookup is treated as base_risk_points 40, high_risk_amount_threshold 0, and embargoed false.
- Risk score starts with the lookup base points. Add 25 for at least 5 failed logins, 20 for at least one chargeback, 15 when transaction_amount exceeds the country threshold, 10 for account_age_days below 14, and 10 for VPN detection. Cap the final score at 100.
- risk_band is CRITICAL at 80 or above, HIGH from 55 through 79, MEDIUM from 30 through 54, and LOW otherwise.
- Any embargoed country, a CRITICAL score, or a HIGH score with a transaction amount greater than 1000 goes to output port 0. All other records go to port 1.
- For manual review, primary_reason precedence is EMBARGOED_COUNTRY, CHARGEBACK_HISTORY, FAILED_LOGINS, HIGH_VALUE_TRANSACTION, NEW_ACCOUNT, VPN, then SCORE_THRESHOLD. masked_device_id is UNKNOWN when device_id is null or empty; otherwise retain only its last four characters and prefix it with ****.
- For auto-clear, clearance_code is LOW_RISK for LOW, STANDARD_CLEAR for MEDIUM, and HIGH_SCORE_BELOW_AMOUNT_GATE for the remaining HIGH records. event_date is the date portion of event_time.

Implementation clarifications:
- Use country_code as the CountryRiskLookup key. 'Embargoed country' means the returned embargoed field is true. 'Country threshold' means returned high_risk_amount_threshold, compared with transaction_amount.
- The risk addends use exactly failed_login_count_24h, chargeback_count_180d, account_age_days, and is_vpn_detected. Apply every qualifying addend, then cap the result at 100 before deriving risk_band and routing.
- A manual-review SCORE_THRESHOLD reason applies only when none of the six earlier primary-reason conditions applies. It refers to the score-based route condition (CRITICAL, or HIGH with transaction_amount > 1000).
- masked_device_id uses device_id. For a nonempty device ID shorter than four characters, retain the entire device ID and still prefix it with ****.

Lookup table definition:
- Lookup table ID: CountryRiskLookup.
- Lookup record metadata ID: CountryRiskLookupMeta.
- Lookup record name: CountryRiskLookup_Record.
- Key field(s): country_code.
- Fields: country_code:string; base_risk_points:integer; high_risk_amount_threshold:decimal; embargoed:boolean.

Write CTL2 for a Reformat/Map component with input port 0 and output port 0.

Input metadata, port 0:
<Metadata id="SupplierProductIn">
  <Record name="SupplierProductIn_Record" type="delimited">
    <Field name="supplier_sku" type="string" nullable="false"/>
    <Field name="supplier_id" type="string" nullable="false"/>
    <Field name="title" type="string" nullable="false"/>
    <Field name="category_path" type="string" nullable="false"/>
    <Field name="base_price" type="decimal" nullable="false"/>
    <Field name="sale_price" type="decimal"/>
    <Field name="stock_on_hand" type="integer" nullable="false"/>
    <Field name="reorder_point" type="integer" nullable="false"/>
    <Field name="attributes_json" type="string"/>
    <Field name="discontinued_at" type="date" format="yyyy-MM-dd"/>
  </Record>
</Metadata>

Lookup metadata: `SupplierPolicyLookup`, keyed by supplier_id, returns supplier_id (string), minimum_margin_pct (decimal), fulfillment_days (integer), and restricted_category_prefixes (string list). A supplier has at most one policy record.

Output metadata, port 0:
<Metadata id="CatalogPublishOut">
  <Record name="CatalogPublishOut_Record" type="delimited">
    <Field name="catalog_key" type="string" nullable="false"/>
    <Field name="display_title" type="string" nullable="false"/>
    <Field name="root_category" type="string" nullable="false"/>
    <Field name="effective_price" type="decimal" nullable="false"/>
    <Field name="stock_status" type="string" nullable="false"/>
    <Field name="estimated_ship_date" type="date" format="yyyy-MM-dd" nullable="false"/>
    <Field name="publish_status" type="string" nullable="false"/>
    <Field name="suppression_reason" type="string"/>
    <Field name="color" type="string"/>
    <Field name="size" type="string"/>
  </Record>
</Metadata>

Business logic:
- Retrieve the supplier policy. If no policy exists, use a 0 minimum margin, 7 fulfillment days, and no restricted category prefixes. catalog_key is supplier_id + '-' + supplier_sku. display_title is the trimmed title in upper case. root_category is the text before the first '/' in category_path; if there is no '/', use category_path itself.
- effective_price is sale_price when it is non-null, greater than zero, and less than base_price; otherwise it is base_price. Round it to two decimals.
- A sale is too deep when its discount from base_price exceeds the policy minimum_margin_pct. In that case it cannot be published. (For example, a 25 minimum margin means the effective price must be at least 75% of base_price.)
- stock_status is DISCONTINUED when discontinued_at is not null, OUT_OF_STOCK at zero or lower stock, LOW_STOCK when stock is positive but no greater than reorder_point, and IN_STOCK otherwise. estimated_ship_date is today plus 0 days for IN_STOCK, plus fulfillment_days for LOW_STOCK, plus twice fulfillment_days for OUT_OF_STOCK, and today for DISCONTINUED.
- attributes_json, when supplied, is a JSON object that can contain string keys color and size. Parse it and map those keys; missing JSON, missing keys, or null values should produce null color/size without failing the transform.
- publish_status is SUPPRESSED when discontinued, when the category begins with a restricted prefix, or when the sale is too deep; it is BACKORDER for OUT_OF_STOCK records not suppressed, and PUBLISHED otherwise. suppression_reason precedence is DISCONTINUED, RESTRICTED_CATEGORY, then MINIMUM_MARGIN. It is null unless publish_status is SUPPRESSED. Emit one record.

Implementation clarifications:
- Use supplier_id as the SupplierPolicyLookup key. 'Category begins with a restricted prefix' means category_path begins with any string in the lookup field restricted_category_prefixes; an absent or empty list has no match.
- The sale discount percentage is ((base_price - effective_price) / base_price) * 100. It is too deep only when base_price is greater than zero and that percentage is strictly greater than the lookup minimum_margin_pct. A nonpositive base_price is not a minimum-margin suppression condition.
- Use the current graph date as the current graph date for estimated_ship_date. The stock-status conditions use discontinued_at, stock_on_hand, and reorder_point in the stated order.
- Parse only a non-null, non-empty attributes_json. If it is malformed or is not a JSON object, treat color and size as null; otherwise read its color and size keys only when their values are strings.

Lookup table definition:
- Lookup table ID: SupplierPolicyLookup.
- Lookup record metadata ID: SupplierPolicyLookupMeta.
- Lookup record name: SupplierPolicyLookup_Record.
- Key field(s): supplier_id.
- Fields: supplier_id:string; minimum_margin_pct:decimal; fulfillment_days:integer; restricted_category_prefixes:string[].

Create a Reformat/Map transformation with one input and one output.

Input metadata: ClaimIn(claim_id:string, member_id:string, service_date:date, received_date:date, procedure_code:string, billed_amount:decimal, deductible_remaining:decimal, coinsurance_pct:decimal, prior_authorization:boolean, network_status:string).
Output metadata: ClaimDecisionOut(claim_id:string, decision:string, denial_reason:string, allowed_amount:decimal, member_responsibility:decimal, plan_payment:decimal, processing_days:integer).

Business logic:
- processing_days is the whole-day difference between received_date and service_date, but never below zero.
- Allowed amount is 80% of billed_amount for IN_NETWORK and 60% otherwise; round it to two decimals.
- Deny with NO_AUTHORIZATION when procedure_code begins with MRI or CT and prior_authorization is false. Deny with INVALID_AMOUNT when billed_amount is zero or below. Deny with LATE_FILING when processing_days exceeds 365. Use that precedence. A denial sets every monetary output to zero.
- Otherwise, deductible applied is the lower of allowed_amount and deductible_remaining. Member responsibility is deductible applied plus coinsurance_pct percent of the remaining allowed amount. plan_payment is allowed_amount minus member responsibility. Round both to two decimals. Decision is PAID when plan_payment is greater than zero; otherwise DEDUCTIBLE_ONLY. denial_reason is null for non-denied claims.

Write a Reformat/Map transformation with one input and one output.

Input metadata: LoyaltyIn(customer_id:string, tier:string, points_balance:long, last_activity_date:date, account_status:string, manual_extension_date:date).
Output metadata: LoyaltyOut(customer_id:string, effective_tier:string, points_to_expire:long, expiry_date:date, action:string, reason:string).

Business logic:
- Use last_activity_date to calculate the normal expiry: 365 days for BASIC, 548 days for SILVER, 730 days for GOLD, and 1095 days for PLATINUM. Any other tier uses BASIC.
- expiry_date is manual_extension_date when it is later than normal expiry; otherwise normal expiry.
- CLOSED accounts expire all positive points immediately on last_activity_date with action CLOSE_ACCOUNT and reason ACCOUNT_CLOSED.
- For non-closed accounts, action is EXPIRE_NOW when expiry_date is before the current graph date, EXPIRING_SOON when expiry_date is within the next 30 calendar days including today, and ACTIVE otherwise. points_to_expire equals the positive points_balance only for EXPIRE_NOW and zero otherwise. reason is INACTIVITY for EXPIRE_NOW, UPCOMING_EXPIRY for EXPIRING_SOON, and null for ACTIVE. effective_tier is upper-case tier, using BASIC for unrecognized values.

Create a Reformat/Map transformation with one input and two outputs: port 0 for matched payments and port 1 for exceptions.

Input metadata: PaymentIn(payment_id:string, invoice_id:string, invoice_total:decimal, payment_amount:decimal, payment_date:date, due_date:date, currency:string, reversal_flag:boolean, remittance_reference:string).
Port 0 metadata: MatchedPaymentOut(payment_id:string, invoice_id:string, match_status:string, applied_amount:decimal, balance_amount:decimal, days_from_due:integer).
Port 1 metadata: PaymentExceptionOut(payment_id:string, invoice_id:string, exception_code:string, exception_amount:decimal, days_from_due:integer).

Business logic:
- days_from_due is the whole-day difference between payment_date and due_date; negative values are allowed.
- Reversed payments always go to port 1 with exception_code REVERSED_PAYMENT and exception_amount equal to payment_amount.
- A null or empty invoice_id goes to port 1 as MISSING_INVOICE. A payment amount at or below zero goes to port 1 as INVALID_PAYMENT_AMOUNT. A currency other than EUR, USD, or GBP goes to port 1 as UNSUPPORTED_CURRENCY. Apply this precedence after reversal.
- Otherwise route to port 0. applied_amount is the lower of payment_amount and invoice_total; balance_amount is invoice_total minus applied_amount. match_status is PAID_IN_FULL when balance_amount is zero, PARTIAL when applied_amount is below invoice_total, and OVERPAYMENT when payment_amount exceeds invoice_total. Round all output amounts to two decimals.

Write a Reformat/Map transformation with one input and one output.

Input metadata: SaleIn(order_id:string, customer_country:string, customer_postal_code:string, product_tax_class:string, net_amount:decimal, ship_date:date).
Lookup table definition:
- Lookup table ID: JurisdictionTaxLookup.
- Lookup record metadata: JurisdictionTax(country:string, postal_prefix:string, standard_rate:decimal, reduced_rate:decimal, digital_rate:decimal, effective_from:date, effective_to:date).
- Key fields are country and postal_prefix. Several records may share a country; choose the matching record whose postal_prefix is the longest prefix of customer_postal_code and whose effective date range includes ship_date. A null effective_to has no end date.
Output metadata: TaxOut(order_id:string, jurisdiction:string, tax_rate:decimal, tax_amount:decimal, tax_status:string).

Business logic:
- If no matching lookup record exists, set jurisdiction to UNRESOLVED, tax_rate and tax_amount to zero, and tax_status to REVIEW.
- Otherwise jurisdiction is country plus - plus postal_prefix. Use reduced_rate for FOOD and BOOK, digital_rate for DIGITAL, and standard_rate for all other product_tax_class values. A null selected rate is zero. tax_amount is net_amount multiplied by tax_rate divided by 100, rounded to two decimals. tax_status is EXEMPT when rate is zero and TAXED otherwise.

Create a Reformat/Map transformation with one input and two outputs: port 0 for allocatable lines and port 1 for holds.

Input metadata: DemandIn(order_line_id:string, warehouse_region:string, sku:string, requested_qty:integer, customer_priority:string, requested_ship_date:date, restricted_goods:boolean).
Lookup table definition:
- Lookup table ID: StockPolicyLookup.
- Lookup record metadata: StockPolicy(region:string, sku:string, available_qty:integer, reserved_qty:integer, daily_allocation_limit:integer, restricted_allowed:boolean, lead_days:integer).
- Key fields are region and sku; at most one record matches.
Port 0 metadata: AllocationOut(order_line_id:string, allocated_qty:integer, backorder_qty:integer, promised_ship_date:date, allocation_class:string).
Port 1 metadata: HoldOut(order_line_id:string, hold_reason:string, requested_qty:integer).

Business logic:
- If no policy matches, send port 1 with hold_reason STOCK_POLICY_MISSING. If restricted_goods is true and restricted_allowed is false, send port 1 with hold_reason RESTRICTED_GOODS. If requested_qty is zero or below, send port 1 with hold_reason INVALID_QUANTITY. Use that precedence.
- Otherwise usable inventory is available_qty minus reserved_qty, floored at zero. allocated_qty is the lower of requested_qty, usable inventory, and daily_allocation_limit. backorder_qty is requested_qty minus allocated_qty.
- promised_ship_date is requested_ship_date when allocated_qty equals requested_qty; otherwise requested_ship_date plus lead_days. allocation_class is FULL for full allocation, PARTIAL for a positive partial allocation, and BACKORDER for zero allocation. Send these records to port 0.
